Answer: D
Reason: The series of chest X-rays demonstrates a progression from initial bilateral alveolar-interstitial opacities (Figure 1) to dense consolidations (Figure 4), followed by complete resolution in the follow-up images (Figures 5a and 5b). This rapid evolution and subsequent clearance are characteristic of pulmonary hemorrhage seen in severe leptospirosis (Weil syndrome), distinguishing it from conditions like Goodpasture's which typically have a more protracted course or bacterial pneumonia which resolves more slowly.
